Yes, this feels right. Typing `closures #reference` left just **JavaScript | MDN** — it understood the `#reference` part as "must have the reference label" and treated "closures" as the word to look for (which it found in my note). That's exactly the mix I was hoping for: a label condition and a plain search word working together in one box.

And both your assumptions match what I'd expect:

- Ignoring capital letters after the `#` is right — `#Reference` or `#REFERENCE` should behave the same as `#reference`. I don't want to have to remember exactly how I capitalized a label.
- Requiring a bookmark to carry all of the labels I type also makes sense to me. If I bother typing two labels, I'm trying to narrow down, so I'd expect "has both," not "has either." (And if I ever want an either/or, that's the "combining conditions" thing I mentioned last time, which is separate.)

So this inline label search is good.
